bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 415850462 (haproxy): Stack-buffer-overflow READ 8 found by fuzz target fuzz_cfg_parser [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/415850462
bug_description.normalized: The staged 131-byte witness is a single configuration line consisting of 66 `0xff` bytes separated by 65 single spaces, with no trailing space or newline. `parse_cfg()` copies that line into `thisline`, creates local stack array `char *args[MAX_LINE_ARGS + 1]`, sets `arg = sizeof(args) / sizeof(*args) = 65`, and calls `parse_line()`. Inside `parse_line()`, `argsmax = *nbargs - 1` reduces writable argument-start slots to 64, so token starts 65 and 66 no longer store into `args[arg]`; the function only records `PARSE_ERR_TOOMANY` and keeps parsing. The 65th separator still increments `arg` to 65, and because the final `0xff` is not followed by whitespace, the end-of-line cleanup runs with `in_arg == 1`. The saved ASan crash on the right-hand operand of `if (!empty_arg_ptr && args[arg] == out + arg_start)` proves `!empty_arg_ptr` was true there, so the code evaluates `args[65]` without checking `arg < argsmax`. ASan reports that read as `stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 8` at `src/tools.c:6493`, one pointer past the caller's 65-slot stack array `args[0..64]` in `parse_cfg()`.

source.description: First project-code read that materializes attacker-controlled bytes as the config line later tokenized by `parse_line()`.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` has sha256 `ffb3b6f94df45cafcb44a86ba0f7ea1f3d43f04bfe04bfcbdfc5a0d43e07a6bb` and length 131 bytes: `ff 20` repeated 65 times, then a final `ff`. This `fgets_from_mem()` call copies that exact byte sequence into `thisline` as one line because the witness has no embedded NUL and no newline terminator.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: The final empty-argument check indexes `args[arg]` without the bounds guard that should require `arg < argsmax` first.
root_cause.note: The staged patch changes this exact condition to `if (!empty_arg_ptr && arg < argsmax && args[arg] == out + arg_start)` and makes the same repair at the analogous reads on lines 6442 and 6484.

sink.description: The crashing read is the evaluation of `args[arg]` in the final end-of-line cleanup.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 8` at `src/tools.c:6493:25` and identifies stack object `args` in `parse_cfg()` as `[608,1128)`, so index 65 begins exactly at the first byte beyond the array.

parser_admitted.description: After leading-space trimming, the witness line is neither empty nor a section header, so `parse_cfg()` sends it directly into `parse_line()`.

fine_trace.code: while (fgets_from_mem(thisline + readbytes, linesize - readbytes, &cur_position, cfg->content + cfg->size)) {
fine_trace.note: `fgets_from_mem()` copies the staged 131-byte witness into mutable line buffer `thisline`. The materialized line is 66 `0xff` bytes separated by 65 single spaces, with no trailing separator or newline.

This local caller stack object is the destination extent later overread. With `MAX_LINE_ARGS == 64`, the array has 65 pointer slots `args[0]` through `args[64]`; ASan reports its frame extent as `[608,1128)`.

depends_on.via: fgets_from_mem(thisline + readbytes, linesize - readbytes, &cur_position, cfg->content + cfg->size)

fine_trace.note: Immediately before the call, `parse_cfg()` passes `*nbargs = 65` into `parse_line()`, i.e. the full length of the caller's `args` table.
`parse_line()` immediately reduces the writable argument-start budget to `argsmax == 64`. Any later token start with `arg >= 64` skips the `args[arg]` store.

The separator-close path increments `arg` once per space. Because the witness alternates one non-space byte and one space 64 times before token 65 begins, these first 64 separator events advance `arg` from 0 to 64.
Token 65 starts with `arg == 64`, so `arg < argsmax` is false. `parse_line()` does not store a start pointer for that token; it only sets `PARSE_ERR_TOOMANY` and continues scanning.
The 65th separator closes token 65 and increments `arg` from 64 to 65. No code clamps `arg` before the final end-of-line cleanup.

The last byte in the witness is a non-space `0xff`, and there is no trailing separator or newline. The final token is therefore still open at end of input, so this cleanup block runs with `in_arg == 1` and the current index still `arg == 65`.

The right-hand `args[arg]` read is reachable only if `!empty_arg_ptr` is true. The saved ASan report faults at `src/tools.c:6493:25`, so C short-circuit evaluation proves `empty_arg_ptr` was still NULL on the crashing execution.

Root cause. The final empty-argument check reuses `arg` as an array index even though the witness has already driven `arg` to 65 and `argsmax` is only 64. The missing `arg < argsmax` guard is exactly what the patch adds.

Sink. Evaluating `args[arg]` with `arg == 65` reads one pointer past the caller's 65-slot stack array. ASan reports a `READ of size 8` at offset 1128, exactly the first byte beyond `args` `[608,1128)` in the `parse_cfg()` frame.

stack_object.name: args
stack_object.note: ASan reports `args` as `[608,1128)` in the `parse_cfg()` frame, so the faulting read at offset 1128 is exactly one 8-byte pointer past the array.

allocation_context.note: The overflowed object is the local stack array `char *args[MAX_LINE_ARGS + 1];` in `parse_cfg()`.

format.name: 131-byte raw config line for `fuzz_cfg_parser`
format.contract: Exactly the staged 131-byte witness with sha256 `ffb3b6f94df45cafcb44a86ba0f7ea1f3d43f04bfe04bfcbdfc5a0d43e07a6bb`: 66 `0xff` bytes separated by 65 single spaces, with no trailing space and no trailing newline (`ff 20` repeated 65 times, then `ff`). The harness admits it because `size >= 50`; `parse_cfg()` copies it as one config line; `parse_line()` advances `arg` on each separator until the 65th space makes `arg == 65`; and the final `if (!empty_arg_ptr && args[arg] == out + arg_start)` then reads `args[65]`. The staged evidence proves this exact witness shape and parser state, not a broader family of lengths or separators.
